$comment: Decision board, not a changelog. `status` is one of: shipped (already live in this build), needs-pick (a choice only you can make, options listed), proposed (queued, nothing done). `review_decision` is left blank on purpose for you to fill; the site renders whatever you put there. `prompt_snippet` is written to be pasted straight into a design brief.

board.title: Lead with buying help, not with the verification process
board.proposal: Front page opens with a lead guide and a 'start here' question module, the four verified listings as a product rail below it, then clusters, then the seasonal note. The register, the gate report and the flag list move to a single footer group called Transparency.
board.why: A buyer arrives with a question about dinner, not about our evidence chain. The register still has to be reachable, but it is a promise kept in the footer, not the front window.
board.effect_on_readers: The first screen answers 'what should I compare'; the fifth screen proves we did not invent anything.
board.risk: low — the audit material is one click away, not removed

options.label: Product-led hero (deals first)
options.tradeoff: Highest intent to click, looks like every other affiliate grid, and we have no prices to show, so it would be four cards with nothing on them.

options.label: Editorial-led front page
options.tradeoff: Reads like a magazine and earns repeat visits; slightly slower to a buy click, which is why the rail sits one scroll down.

options.label: Hybrid, as shipped
options.tradeoff: Editorial above the fold, product rail in the first two scrolls, transparency in the footer. Chosen.

board.recommended: Hybrid, as shipped
board.prompt_snippet: Design a publication front page: one lead story with a one-sentence deck, a 'start here' question list, a horizontal product rail with status chips, then two cluster cards, then a seasonal note. Warm paper background, ink text, one accent colour, hairline rules, no gradient hero, no stock photo of a smiling person holding a spatula.

board.title: Keep the disclosure above the fold on every page, including the front page
board.proposal: A strip directly under the masthead on all pages carrying the required statement, a plain-English sentence about what that means for the reader, and a link to /disclosure/. The same statement repeats in the footer. Every product link carries '(paid link)'.
board.why: Amazon's help page requires the statement clearly and conspicuously on the site and link-level disclosure near each link; the FTC rule behind it is about the reader noticing. Both are placement duties, and placement is checkable in build.
board.effect_on_readers: Nobody has to scroll to the footer to learn we get paid, which is the single most trust-building thing an affiliate page can do.
board.risk: if it were missing, the account is at risk; nothing about having it hurts

options.label: Footer only
options.tradeoff: What most sites do; Amazon's help text explicitly says readers shouldn't have to hunt for it.

options.label: Strip under the masthead plus footer, as shipped
options.tradeoff: Visible on every page load, one line of height. Chosen.

options.label: Interstitial 'before you click' modal
options.tradeoff: Maximally conspicuous, measurably annoying, and it can suppress the clicks we are trying to earn.

board.recommended: Strip plus footer, as shipped
board.prompt_snippet: Add a disclosure strip below the masthead on every page: single line, accent-tinted background, 13-14px type, statement plus one plain sentence plus a link to the disclosure page. Do not dim it, do not make it dismissible.

board.title: Type and palette: paper and ink, not the affiliate default
board.proposal: Ship the system stack now (ui-serif display, system-ui body, three greys plus one paprika accent, no webfont request). When the domain question (S-15) is settled, self-host one display face and one text face, subset, preloaded.
board.why: The current look reads generated because it uses the same three ingredients every template uses: a gradient, a card grid, and Inter. A serif with real type scale and one warm accent is the cheapest distance from that. Self-hosting rather than a CDN keeps the first paint on the critical path and adds no third party to a privacy page that promises no trackers.
board.effect_on_readers: Faster first paint on a phone, and a page that looks like a title rather than a funnel.
board.effort: now: done · later: half a day
board.cost: 0 now; a licence only if you want a paid face
board.risk: low

options.label: System stack only
options.tradeoff: Zero requests, renders differently per device, slightly less owned. Shipped in this build.

options.label: One self-hosted display face
options.tradeoff: Real identity, ~30KB with a subset, one build step. Recommended next move.

options.label: Google Fonts CDN
options.tradeoff: Fastest to do and it is the exact texture of a template site, plus a third-party request a privacy page has to explain.

board.recommended: Ship the system stack now; add one self-hosted display face at the domain step
board.prompt_snippet: Use a serif for headlines at a 1.25 type scale, sans-serif for body at 17px/1.6, a warm off-white background, near-black text, one paprika accent used only for links, chips and the CTA. No gradients, no glassmorphism, no drop shadows above 8% opacity.

board.title: Product data: keep prices and ratings off the page until an authorized feed exists
board.proposal: Publish identity, category and seller-titled attributes with capture dates, and let the marketplace show the live price. Revisit only when PA-API credentials exist (Q-05).
board.why: A price copied from a listing page is a screenshot of yesterday. It goes stale silently, it undercuts trust the first time the reader sees a different number, and Google's product rich-result documentation ties presentation to exactly the fields we cannot keep current.
board.effect_on_readers: Nobody is told a number we cannot stand behind.
board.effort: 0 now · 1-2 days to wire an API refresh after access
board.risk: showing no price may cost some clicks; showing a wrong one costs the reader

options.label: Never publish prices
options.tradeoff: Clean and honest; costs the 'from $X' affordance. Current state.

options.label: PA-API refresh on a schedule, price with a timestamp
options.tradeoff: Best of both, blocked on credentials; also obliges us to refresh weekly or delete the field.

options.label: Scrape prices into the build
options.tradeoff: Do not choose this. It is the fastest route to a banned account and to being wrong.

board.recommended: Never publish prices until an authorized feed exists, then publish with a timestamp
board.prompt_snippet: In each product card, replace the price slot with a live-price button labelled 'Check the listing on Amazon (paid link)' and a caption reading 'Price shown by Amazon at click time; we do not store it.'

board.title: Artwork: own it, and say where it came from
board.proposal: Use generated editorial artwork — line-and-shape illustrations of baskets, doors, cavities, probes — with a caption on every page naming them as illustration, not product photography. No Amazon imagery, no stock photography.
board.why: Listing photos are licensed through program tooling, not free to hotlink, and a scraped image is both a rights problem and the visual signature of a boiler-room affiliate site. Drawn diagrams also do a better job of the actual editorial point, which is about size and clearance.
board.effect_on_readers: The page has a face that is not a manufacturer's render, and the caption prevents the art from being read as evidence.
board.risk: low, as long as captions stay

options.label: Generated editorial illustration, as shipped
options.tradeoff: Owned, consistent, obviously not photographic once captioned.

options.label: Program-licensed product images via API
options.tradeoff: What a real shop does; blocked on Q-05.

options.label: No imagery
options.tradeoff: Fastest and safest, and it makes a lifestyle purchase feel like a spreadsheet.

board.recommended: Illustration now, licensed product imagery when the API does
board.prompt_snippet: Commission a consistent set of technical illustrations: single basket, twin basket, oven-style cavity with French doors, and a probe inserted at the thickest point. Two colours on paper, thin strokes, dimension ticks, no photorealism, no text baked into the image.

board.title: Replace ambiguous outbound links with tagged Special Links, and prove one before scaling
board.proposal: Rewrite every outbound link to https://www.amazon.com/dp/<observed-id>?tag=shopnow047c-20 with rel="sponsored nofollow", and mark each link pending-test in the UI until the in-account click report confirms it. Do not claim the supplied link.amazon forms are invalid; their status is FLG-003.
board.why: Amazon's Special Links clause requires the tag as a URL parameter. Our capture of the four resolved destinations showed parameters for channel, button and language and no tag at all, which is a lost-commission shape regardless of what the policy says.
board.effect_on_readers: Identical destination; the reader cannot tell and does not need to.
board.risk: the tag string itself is unverified in-account (FLG-009), so the proof step is not optional

options.label: Tagged long links, as shipped
options.tradeoff: Verifiable in the page source, no redirect layer, nothing hidden.

options.label: Branded /go/ redirect that appends the tag
options.tradeoff: Prettier and ownable; adds a hop whose policy status we cannot settle here. See S-06a below.

options.label: Keep the supplied link.amazon codes
options.tradeoff: Zero work, and every capture we took showed no tag at the destination.

board.recommended: Tagged long links; test one per product in-account; only then consider /go/
board.prompt_snippet: Style the outbound link as a filled button with a small '(paid link)' label on the same line, and append a 12px caption 'Opens Amazon.com in a new tab · tagged with our associate ID'. Keep the href honest in the status bar: no wrapper domain.

board.title: Whether to add a branded redirect layer at all
board.proposal: Keep it off until Pages is replaced by a host that can run a redirect, and until FLG-003 is settled by a human who has read the current agreement.
board.why: A redirect layer only buys link swapping without a rebuild and tidy click attribution. Both are real, and both are worth less than a policy question mark over every link on the site while the site is still small enough to rebuild in seconds.
board.effect_on_readers: None today; later it means a hover target that does not obviously say Amazon, which is precisely the thing to be careful about.
board.effort: half a day when a host exists
board.risk: medium — cloaking is the classic grounds for account closure

options.label: No redirect layer (current)
options.tradeoff: Rebuilds instead of redirects. Chosen.

options.label: Redirect with the tag appended and the destination stated in the anchor text
options.tradeoff: Acceptable under a permissive reading; needs the agreement read first.

options.label: Redirect with the destination hidden
options.tradeoff: Do not choose this.

board.recommended: Off until a host and a policy read both exist

board.title: Structured data: ship what we can support, hold the rest
board.proposal: Emit WebSite, Organization, Article and BreadcrumbList on the relevant pages. Do not emit Product, Review or aggregateRating until an authorized offer feed and a genuine review process exist.
board.why: Google's product documentation connects this markup to price, availability and ratings. We publish none of those deliberately. Marking up a review for a machine nobody cooked with is the kind of thing that turns a small site into a policy example.
board.effect_on_readers: Search sees an accurately typed document instead of an over-decorated one.
board.risk: we give up rich-result garnish, which we have not earned

options.label: Article + Breadcrumb only, as shipped
options.tradeoff: Honest, minimal.

options.label: Add Product with name and URL only
options.tradeoff: Technically allowed, delivers no enhancement without the missing fields; adds no value and one more thing to audit.

options.label: Add FAQPage from our own questions
options.tradeoff: Consider later; FAQ rich results were restricted to prominent authoritative sites in 2023, so it is decoration with a caveat we have not verified this session.

board.recommended: Article + Breadcrumb, revisit after S-04

board.title: Verify Search Console before the second week of publishing
board.proposal: Add the verification token to config, rebuild, submit docs/sitemap.xml, and let eight weeks of queries decide the next four topics instead of the queue in the front page.
board.why: The brief's own rule is that the next topic is chosen from measured queries. Without a property there is no measurement, and every topic after this one is a guess dressed as a strategy.
board.effect_on_readers: Invisible today, and the reason the site gets better on schedule.
board.risk: none

options.label: URL-prefix property with a meta tag on Pages
options.tradeoff: Works with no DNS control. Recommended while the host is undecided.

options.label: Domain property with a DNS TXT record
options.tradeoff: Covers every subdomain and future host move; needs a domain (S-15).

options.label: Also submit to Bing Webmaster
options.tradeoff: Two extra minutes, an import-from-Google option, and a second opinion on indexing.

board.recommended: Meta-tag property now, domain property when the domain exists
board.prompt_snippet: Add a verification meta tag block to the head template, driven by data/config.json → search_console.verification_token, and only emit it when the token is non-empty so the gate can prove the unverified state.

board.title: Point the click beacon at a collector you own
board.proposal: Run tools/collector.py on any small host, set measurement.endpoint in config, and rebuild. Five event names, no IPs, no cookies, opt-out respected, append-only JSONL that the ledger ingests.
board.why: Outbound clicks are the only conversion signal an affiliate site has before Amazon's report, and a self-hosted line keeps it out of a consent banner. GitHub Pages cannot run it, so the build ships armed-but-off rather than pretending it is counting.
board.effect_on_readers: None — that is the point of a first-party counter with no identifiers.
board.cost: free tier to about $5 a month
board.risk: collecting nothing is a choice with a cost of its own: no evidence for any future decision

options.label: Self-hosted stdlib collector, as shipped but unarmed
options.tradeoff: Full control, no consent banner load, and you maintain a process.

options.label: A hosted privacy-first analytics product
options.tradeoff: Dashboards for free-ish, another party and another line in the privacy page.

options.label: GA4
options.tradeoff: Powerful, and it makes the privacy page longer and the banner bigger than the disclosure.

options.label: Nothing, and read Associates Central only
options.tradeoff: Perfectly defensible at this size; you lose which guide caused the click.

board.recommended: Self-hosted collector; it is already written

board.title: Reader capture: be honest that there is none
board.proposal: Keep the form disabled with a sentence that says so (shipped), or pick a list provider and connect it. A form that swallows an address into a static host is how a site loses a reader's trust permanently.
board.why: Email is the only audience an affiliate site owns through a core update, and it is also the one place where a broken form does damage out of proportion to its size.
board.effect_on_readers: Right now: an explanation instead of a black hole.
board.cost: free tier to about $20 a month
board.risk: collecting addresses without storage is the only genuinely bad option

options.label: Disabled with a mailto fallback, as shipped
options.tradeoff: No list, no lie.

options.label: Hosted newsletter service with a double opt-in
options.tradeoff: Real owned audience; adds a third-party form and a privacy line.

options.label: Own collector endpoint for signups
options.tradeoff: Same host as S-09, no vendor, and now you run a list including its unsubscribe law.

board.recommended: Decide with S-09, same host, one vendor fewer

board.title: Put a human name on it, or never write 'we tested'
board.proposal: Keep the desk byline and the sentence that says no product was tested until a person is named with credentials and a contact route. Then, and only then, add 'reviewed by' lines and author markup.
board.why: The fastest way to read like generated content is an invented authority. The gate already refuses 'we tested', 'our experts' and 'editor's choice' — that ban is only safe while the byline stays institutional.
board.effect_on_readers: A reader can tell exactly who is responsible for a claim, which is what a byline is for.
board.risk: naming a person makes them answerable; that is the point

options.label: Desk byline only, as shipped
options.tradeoff: Honest and thin on authority.

options.label: Named editor, no testing claims
options.tradeoff: Adds real accountability without changing what the site can say about products.

options.label: Named tester who actually cooks in them
options.tradeoff: The only route to genuine review copy, and it costs a machine per reviewer plus real hours.

board.recommended: Named editor now, tester only if the budget exists

board.title: Keep the comparison static and crawlable, not a JavaScript widget
board.proposal: Ship the comparison as a real table in the HTML (done) with an optional client-side picker that only filters the same rows. The picker is currently a plain two-select form that navigates, so nothing depends on it.
board.why: A widget that builds the comparison in memory gives the reader a nicer click and gives the crawler an empty page. Filtering a server-rendered table keeps both.
board.effect_on_readers: Works with JavaScript off, works in a text browser, works on a bad connection.
board.risk: low

options.label: Static table with a filter form, as shipped
options.tradeoff: Chosen.

options.label: Full interactive comparator with saved state
options.tradeoff: Worth building once real traffic exists; measure first (S-09).

board.recommended: Static with filter; defer the app-like comparator

board.title: Run the season we are in
board.proposal: It is late November: the front page carries a doneness angle and the thermometer, because that is what a reader is buying this fortnight, and the cluster pages say which guides are seasonal and which are evergreen.
board.why: Seasonal fit is one of the few levers an unranked new site has: the query exists this month, the giants are slow to refresh, and 'what temperature is turkey done' is exactly the question our one non-air-fryer listing answers. A publication notices the calendar; a content farm does not.
board.effect_on_readers: The site looks alive and timely on the day it is discovered.
board.risk: seasonal pages need retiring; the staleness rule (S-18) covers it

options.label: Run the season, as shipped
options.tradeoff: Chosen, with a retirement date on the module.

options.label: Evergreen only
options.tradeoff: Less maintenance, and a new site competes with ten-year-old pages on their best day.

options.label: Prime Day / Black Friday event pages
options.tradeoff: Highest volume, and product-list pages need additional original content under the policies clause; also event links have placement rules we have not read in-account.

board.recommended: Seasonal module now, event pages only after Q-02 is answered

board.title: A second commission line, later
board.proposal: Once measured clicks exist, evaluate direct brand programs and Creator Connections against the same pages, and keep whichever pays per visit instead of adding links everywhere.
board.why: One manufacturer's listing at an ambiguous 1.25% or 3.00% is a thin business. The comparison is only sound with data on what a visit is worth, which is why this is a later row and not an early one.
board.effect_on_readers: None if done right; a page with three competing buy buttons is worse for the reader and for trust.
board.risk: disclosure complexity grows with every program added to a page

options.label: Amazon only until clicks are measured
options.tradeoff: Chosen for now.

options.label: Add one brand program on the matching product page only
options.tradeoff: Best margin per click, more disclosure text on that page.

options.label: Join a large network now
options.tradeoff: Inventory breadth nobody here has asked for yet.

board.recommended: Wait for measured clicks

board.title: Get a domain before the site earns anything
board.proposal: A github.io subpath is fine for launch and wrong for an asset. Move to a real domain, keep /Affil3 as a redirect for one year, and let the canonical set follow the new host in the same commit.
board.why: Canonical URLs, the sitemap, the feed and every share live in the address bar. Changing host after traffic arrives costs most of the benefit; the change costs about a dollar and an afternoon now. It also unlocks the collector and reader capture on the same origin.
board.effect_on_readers: A name a person can remember and trust.
board.risk: the name is hard to change later, so pick deliberately

options.label: Stay on Pages for now
options.tradeoff: Zero cost, zero brand equity. Where we are.

options.label: Buy a category wordmark domain
options.tradeoff: Memorable, ownable, needs a name you will not resent in two years. Site ships as 'Counterwise' in this build for that reason.

options.label: Buy a keyword domain (airfryerguides…)
options.tradeoff: Exact-match domains have carried no special weight for a long time, and it boxes the niche in forever.

board.recommended: Brandable domain, this quarter, before promotion starts

board.title: No video, no social channels, until something is measured
board.proposal: Hold every channel that costs recurring effort. Revisit when the metrics page has 30 days of clicks and Search Console shows which query the traffic came from.
board.why: Short-form video is the highest-effort, slowest-to-attribute channel available to a two-listing operation. Deciding to do it because it is what affiliate sites do is exactly the instinct-first pattern this project is supposed to break.
board.effect_on_readers: None.
board.risk: opportunity cost, which the ledger will show

options.label: Hold (recommended)
options.tradeoff: Nothing spent, nothing learned.

options.label: One 60-second clip per guide, unlisted
options.tradeoff: Cheap experiment; still a permanent production habit once it works.

board.recommended: Hold

board.title: Put a scale rule on page creation, in the gate
board.proposal: Automate collection, formatting, verification and measurement. Gate new pages: one page per buying question a real reader asked, and never more than two pages per question.
board.why: Google's scaled content abuse policy targets many pages generated primarily to rank, however they are made — which is precisely the failure mode of an 'AI-powered affiliate platform'. The automation brief and the spam policy collide here, and the only durable answer is to automate the research and the plumbing instead of the word count.
board.effect_on_readers: Fewer pages, each with a reason to exist.
board.effort: policy choice, then a 20-line gate rule
board.risk: growing slower than a spammy competitor, for a while

options.label: Hard cap: one guide per verified question, 2 per week
options.tradeoff: Recommended. Slow and defensible; the cadence file already assumes it.

options.label: Soft target with quarterly pruning of pages with zero impressions
options.tradeoff: Faster growth; pruning without Search Console data is blind, so it depends on S-08.

options.label: Generate for the long tail first, refine later
options.tradeoff: The classic 2019 playbook. It is now an explicitly named abuse pattern and the worst available choice for a new domain.

board.recommended: Hard cap now, soft target only after eight weeks of queries
board.prompt_snippet: Add a build gate rule: fail if the guide count grows by more than 2 per week, if two guides share a normalized question stem, or if a guide cites fewer than two sources that resolve to a registered source ID.

board.title: A 90-day staleness rule on every observation
board.proposal: A scheduled run of tools/resolve_links.py re-captures each listing title, path identifier and breadcrumb, writes a dated record, and the build stamps every gear and guide page with its capture date. Anything older than 90 days gets a visible 'data older than 90 days' notice, not a silent delete.
board.why: Titles, accessories and category placement change without telling anyone. The dangerous state is not being wrong on day one; it is being right on day one and stale on day four hundred, with no marker on the page.
board.effect_on_readers: The reader can see how old our evidence is, which is the only honest freshness signal available.
board.risk: an unattended fetch that starts failing will look like silence; the job must post its own status

options.label: Adopt 90 days, as proposed
options.tradeoff: Chosen default.

options.label: Re-capture on every build
options.tradeoff: Freshest, but the CI job needs network access to a site that rate-limits bots.

options.label: Manual refresh only
options.tradeoff: What most small sites actually do, which is why most small sites are wrong.

board.recommended: 90 days, with the notice rendered on the page

board.title: Teach the voice in the gate, not in the prompt
board.proposal: Keep the banned-vocabulary list in the build gate and let it fail the site: no 'we tested', no 'editor's choice', no 'best overall', no invented numbers, and none of the filler that signals generated text — 'seamless', 'curated', 'delve', 'unlock', 'elevate', 'look no further', 'in today's fast-paced'.
board.why: Voice instructions decay the moment a model gets tired; a build rule does not. Anything a reader can smell as filler costs credibility on every other sentence on the page, and the only defence that survives automation is a mechanical one.
board.effect_on_readers: Sentences that carry information instead of throat-clearing.
board.risk: a banlist can over-reach; every entry has a `why` and can be waived per page with a reason

options.label: Banlist in the gate, as shipped
options.tradeoff: Chosen.

options.label: Style guide for humans only
options.tradeoff: Does not survive automation, which is the whole premise here.

options.label: Also add a readability floor
options.tradeoff: Worth it later; short sentences are easier to trust, and it is a cheap rule to add.

board.recommended: Keep the banlist; add a readability floor once there is more prose

board.title: Privacy page, 404 and the boring furniture, now rather than after
board.proposal: Ship a short privacy page that matches what the code actually does (no cookies, no stored addresses, no third-party requests), a real 404 that points at the three useful places, and a manifest that records what was built from which inputs.
board.why: A site asking for nothing and storing nothing can say so in eight lines, and saying it is what separates a shop from a funnel. The 404 is where a reader decides whether the site is finished.
board.effect_on_readers: A page that reads like someone lives here.
board.risk: a privacy page must be updated if S-09 or S-10 changes; the gate checks that collecting and privacy stay consistent

options.label: Ship it, as done
options.tradeoff: Chosen.

options.label: Generator from a policy wizard
options.tradeoff: Boilerplate the reader recognises as boilerplate.

board.recommended: Keep the short one, update it the day collection turns on

board.title: Give the buyer one decision to make per page
board.proposal: Every guide ends with a three-line 'what to do next': the checklist to run, the gear row that matches, the one link. No end-of-article wall of related posts.
board.why: An affiliate page's job is a decision, and a reader who finishes with four options usually takes none. Related-post grids are also the layout that most reliably says 'generated'.
board.effect_on_readers: One action, from a page that just earned the right to suggest it.
board.risk: fewer internal clicks per page, which the event schema will measure rather than assume

options.label: One next step, as shipped
options.tradeoff: Chosen.

options.label: Related grid
options.tradeoff: More pageviews, less decision.

board.recommended: One next step

board.title: Publish the gate report next to the content it polices
board.proposal: The build writes a machine-readable report of which rules passed and what each one checks, rendered as a page. Anyone can see that a rule exists, runs, and can fail.
board.why: 'The machinery is trustworthy' is not a claim you can make about a private script. A public report with the rule text attached is the nearest thing to proof a static site can offer.
board.effect_on_readers: A buyer who wants to check our work can check the checker.
board.risk: it also publishes the gaps, which is intended

options.label: Publish it, as shipped
options.tradeoff: Chosen.

options.label: CI logs only
options.tradeoff: Invisible to readers, so worth less as a promise.

board.recommended: Publish
